correctness.rationale: The domain is the spherical zonal harmonic h_t=1+t(z^3−3z/5) with |t|<=1/2 and an arbitrary unit axis in R3. The exact principal radii 1−2tz^3 and 1+t(6z−8z^3) and the global cubic extrema +/-2 establish both necessity and sufficiency of convexity. Restricting to each great circle separates the first translation harmonic from amplitude t*tau^3/4 in the third harmonic; integrating p^2−(pprime)^2 gives b_t(v)=pi(1−t^2(1−(e dot v)^2)^3/4) for all v. The normalized random law follows from e dot V uniform[-1,1], with t!=0. Applying the spherical support-function volume identity to b_t produces a polynomial with coefficients −12/35,−32/1001,+640/46189; its derivative is strictly negative on t in (0,1/2] and its sharp endpoint factor is 1475168/1616615. Original-body area/volume match direct curvature integration and Cauchy averaging. Exact symbolic checks ran successfully from the standalone embedded verify.py; the continuous proof is analytic and does not rely on finite sampling. At t=0 the normalized random variable is excluded, and endpoint bodies are included by semidefinite support-function criterion.

originality.rationale: The full 14-page source arXiv:2609.27192v1 proves the existence of 3-fold symmetric planar projections from cubic supports, but does not determine the axial zonal harmonic convexity interval, exact projection-body volume, or full random-brightness distribution. A published classification establishes that such exceptions are cubic-harmonic support functions without a projection-body volume computation. A published tetrahedral cubic threshold pertains to the rotationally inequivalent harmonic u1*u2*u3. These objects cannot be transformed into each other by rotation, since the axial cubic has a continuous rotation stabilizer and the tetrahedral cubic does not. No stronger indexed exact result was found. Full text of a plausible random-brightness paper was unavailable, and unindexed overlap remains a risk.

value.rationale: The axially invariant cubic is the unique zonal member, up to scale, of the natural degree-three exceptional support space in the new planar-projection symmetry theorem, rather than an arbitrary slice. Exact brightness, projection-body volume and the random-direction law are natural tomography invariants. The complete sextic volume polynomial with a sharp monotonic endpoint ratio, coupled to a scale-free universal random-brightness density and identifiability of the axial amplitude, supplies a reproducible smooth-body benchmark for current geometric-statistical and projection-body research. The previously published tetrahedral convexity calculation concerns a different cubic orbit. The result does not claim a global inequality or merely rename that prior parameter; it solves an exact motivated natural invariant across the full sharp convex admissibility interval. Residual bibliographic risks are disclosed.
